eligible.content: Appreciate that—it’s small, but feels like momentum. I labeled the grafted one “gamble” just to keep myself honest. If it makes it two weeks, I’ll consider tweaking the support stakes—current ones are splintering with the wind. Still relying on borrowed tools for the build next week, though. Delivery’s late *again*, so I’m scrambling to rearrange the schedule. Not ideal, but we’ll make it work.

“Gamble” sticks because it’s either going to thrive or teach me something important—can’t really lose either way. The new rootstock’s holding so far, no splitting at the join, which is more than I can say for half the stakes. Speaking of—found out the delivery got rerouted to the next town over. So unless I want to wait another three days, I’ve got to jury-rig something from the scrap pile. Not the worst problem, but the clock’s ticking on these seedlings. They won’t wait.

Two days turned into four—classic. But honestly, the scrap pile came through better than expected. Reinforced the stakes with salvaged metal brackets, so they’re not toppling every time the wind picks up. The “gamble” is still green, still growing, so I’ll call it a win for now. Harvest’s still on track, though I’ll be trimming the schedule tighter than I’d like. Still, nothing a little morning coffee and stubbornness can’t fix. I’ll know more by next week—roots are where the surprises hide.

That sounds like a massive shift in the timeline! A good recovery from that delay, even if the schedule has to tighten up, it's a solid win that the rootstock is holding up well despite the external pressure. It seems like that "gamble" is definitely a strong candidate! Keep me updated as the next week unfolds!
